correctness.rationale: The blockwise proof is complete for every finite connected threshold graph. For a singleton in a one-block, later zero-blocks of size at least two give an invariant false-twin obstruction, while singleton later zero-blocks are forced sequentially. Vertices in later zero-blocks stall immediately, and the first zero-block has the stated necessary-and-sufficient size condition. A direct definition-level verifier agrees on all 22,528 singleton placements in all 2,047 connected creation sequences of order at most 12.

value.rationale: The scalar value \(\gamma_P(G)=1\) is easy, but the complete set of optimal PMU locations is not: nonuniversal vertices can also be optimal according to a precise creation-block suffix rule. The theorem gives a natural exact classification and multiplicity useful for placement flexibility and for checking or benchmarking threshold-graph power-domination algorithms.
